title: Local residue Galois surjectivity and compatibility with constants
statement: Let $C_0/k_0$ be a curve in the sense of [d-real-setup], with fixed algebraic closure $k$ of the finite field $k_0$. Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a nonempty open with finite complement $S_0$ and let $s\in S_0$. Put $k_s=\kappa(s)$ and $K_s=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathcal O_{C_0,s}^{h})$, using henselization as in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Choose an algebraic closure $\overline K_s$, a compatible algebraic closure of $k_s$, and the residue homomorphism $r_s:D_s=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline K_s/K_s)\to G_s=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{k_s}/k_s)$ of [lem-real-boundary-decomposition-landing]. Identify $\overline{k_s}$ with $k$ over $k_0$, so that $k_s$ is the unique subfield of $k$ with $|k_s|$ elements. Let $\bar u$ be a geometric base point on $U_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\theta_s:D_s\to\pi_1(U_0,\bar u)$ be any decomposition homomorphism obtained from an etale path as in [lem-real-boundary-decomposition-landing]. Let $p:\pi_1(U_0,\bar u)\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ be the arithmetic projection defining the Weil group in [def-wf-weil-group], and let $\iota_s:\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_s)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ be inclusion. Then $k_s/k_0$ is a finite extension of positive degree, $r_s$ is surjective and $p\circ\theta_s=\iota_s\circ r_s$. In particular $p(\theta_s(D_s))=\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_s)$ as a subgroup of $\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$.

proof.text: The projection $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k\to C_0$ is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Thus $C$ is nonempty, and its connectedness in [d-real-setup] implies connectedness of $C_0$ by taking the continuous surjective image. Both schemes have finite type over their respective fields: for $C$, tensor the finitely many generators of each chart in a finite affine cover of $C_0$. Both are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. By the affine characterization in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](1), $C$ as well as $C_0$ is smooth over its field. Their local rings are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. Apply [rem-pc-regular-normal](3) to each: both are irreducible; (1) also makes them normal, hence integral.

source.place: first paragraph, residue Galois surjectivity and arithmetic degree image

proof.text: The nonempty open $U_0$ contains the generic point of the irreducible $C_0$. A nongeneric point of this one-dimensional scheme is closed: a further strict specialization would give, after adjoining the generic point, a chain of length two. Thus $s$ is closed. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), $k_s/k_0$ is finite, of degree $e_s\geq1$, and $|k_s|=q^{e_s}$. The local ring $A=\mathcal O_{C_0,s}$ is regular by Step 1 and has dimension exactly one: the generic point and $s$ give a chain of length one in its spectrum, and any longer chain contradicts $\dim C_0=1$. Therefore $A$ is a DVR by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. Also $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$ is a nonempty open in $C$: it contains the chosen $\bar u$. Any two nonempty relatively open subsets intersect because $C$ is irreducible, so $U$ is irreducible and connected. Finally $U_0$ is quasi-compact since $C_0$ is Noetherian, is locally of finite type by its affine charts, and is separated by restricting the diagonal of $C_0$. Hence it is separated of finite type and geometrically connected, as required for the arithmetic-projection interface.

source.place: first paragraph, residue Galois surjectivity and arithmetic degree image

proof.text: Write $H=A^{\mathrm h}$ and $K=K_s$. By [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], $H$ is henselian local. Its residue field is canonically $k_s$: the field $k_s$ is henselian (idempotent lifting modulo its zero maximal ideal is the identity), so the universal property gives a local map $H\to k_s$ extending $A\to k_s$. The induced composite $k_s\to\kappa(H)\to k_s$ is the identity. The second arrow is an injective field map whose image contains all of $k_s$, so the two arrows are inverse. Apply [lem-real-henselian-residue-galois-action] to $H\to K\subset\overline K_s$. It gives the local integral closure $B$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, the closure $\bar\kappa=B/\mathfrak n$ of $k_s$, the map $r_s$, and the equivariant isomorphism $t:k'\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar\kappa$, where $k'$ is the field of constants algebraic over $k_0$ in $\overline K_s$.

source.place: first paragraph, residue Galois surjectivity and arithmetic degree image

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-strict-henselian-fraction-inertia] to the DVR $A$ of Step 2. It gives domains $H\subset R=A^{\mathrm{sh}}\subset\Omega$, with $\Omega$ a separable closure of $K=\operatorname{Frac}H$, residue field $\kappa(R)=k_s^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and a surjection $\mathrm{res}:\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)\to\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa(R)/k_s)$. Choose $\Omega$ to be the separable algebraic elements of the given $\overline K_s$. Restriction $D_s\to\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)$ is a bijection, including in characteristic $p$: every algebraic $x$ has $x^{p^n}\in\Omega$ for some $n$, by removing all powers of $T^p$ from its irreducible polynomial over $K$ until the derivative is nonzero. An automorphism $\tau$ of $\Omega/K$ extends uniquely by sending $x$ to the unique $p^n$-th root of $\tau(x^{p^n})$ in $\overline K_s$; the formulas for sums and products follow after taking a common $p$-power, and the inverse is the extension of $\tau^{-1}$. Every finite extension of the finite field $k_s$ is separable by [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius], so $\kappa(R)$ is an algebraic closure, just like $\bar\kappa$. The surjection just cited is applied to $A$, whose DVR hypothesis was proved, rather than assuming a DVR property for $H$.

source.place: first paragraph, residue Galois surjectivity and arithmetic degree image

proof.text: Here is the comparison of the residue fields in Step 4 with reduction in $B$. The ring $R$ is henselian local by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure]. For each $n\geq1$, all $q^n$ roots of $T^{q^n}-T$ in the algebraically closed $\kappa(R)$ are simple, since the derivative is $-1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting] they lift to $q^n$ distinct roots in $R\subset\Omega$. A polynomial of degree $q^n$ has no further roots in $\overline K_s$. Every element of $k'$ belongs to a finite field and is such a root for some $n$, so $k'\subset R$. Reduction $u:k'\to\kappa(R)$ is injective, as a unital map out of a field, and surjective, since every element of $\kappa(R)$ is algebraic over a finite field and the same lifting argument supplies its preimage in $k'$. Applying that argument in $H$, whose residue has $q^{e_s}$ elements, shows that all roots of $T^{q^{e_s}}-T$ lie in $H$. Their reductions in $B$ identify this subfield with $k_s$ via $t$, and their reductions in $R$ give the same structural $k_s$. Thus $\beta=t\circ u^{-1}:\kappa(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar\kappa$ is an isomorphism over $k_s$, and $\beta(u(b))=t(b)$ for every $b\in k'$. This chooses the compatible residue identification explicitly.

source.place: first paragraph, residue Galois surjectivity and arithmetic degree image

proof.text: For $\sigma\in D_s$ put $\tau=\sigma|_\Omega$. By [lem-wf-strict-henselian-fraction-inertia], $\tau$ preserves $R$ and reduces there to $\mathrm{res}(\tau)$. Hence $\mathrm{res}(\tau)u(b)=u(\sigma b)$ for $b\in k'$. In $B$, [lem-real-henselian-residue-galois-action] gives $r_s(\sigma)t(b)=t(\sigma b)$. Since $\beta u=t$ and $t$ is surjective, these equalities prove $\beta\,\mathrm{res}(\sigma|_\Omega)\,\beta^{-1}=r_s(\sigma)$ on all of $\bar\kappa$. Consequently $r_s$ is surjective, by the restriction bijection and the strict-henselian surjection in Step 4. This identifies the actual reduction in the algebraic closure, rather than merely an abstract isomorphic quotient.

source.place: first paragraph, residue Galois surjectivity and arithmetic degree image

proof.text: Use the chosen $k_0$-identification $\bar\kappa\simeq k$ to regard $t$ as a map $k'\to k$. Fix $\sigma\in D_s$ and put $g=\iota_s(r_s(\sigma))\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$. For a finite subextension $L/k_0$ of $k/k_0$, let $P_L=U_0\times_{k_0}\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $\rho=g|_L$. The extension $L/k_0$ is Galois with cyclic group generated by $q$-power Frobenius, by [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius]; in particular $g$ preserves $L$. By [lem-real-boundary-decomposition-landing], local fibre points of $P_L$ are embeddings $\lambda:L\to k'$ and $a_{\sigma,P_L}(\lambda)=\sigma\circ\lambda$. Equivariance of $t$ from [lem-real-henselian-residue-galois-action] gives $t\sigma\lambda=g\,t\lambda$. Each embedding $t\lambda:L\to k$ has image $L$: its elements are the roots of $T^{|L|}-T$, which already has all $|L|$ roots in $L$. Its restriction is therefore an element of the same cyclic group, so $g\,t\lambda=t\lambda\,\rho$. Thus $a_{\sigma,P_L}(\lambda)=\lambda\rho$. This is exactly the action on the local fibre of the deck transformation $b_L=\operatorname{id}_{U_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ of $P_L$.

source.place: first paragraph, residue Galois surjectivity and arithmetic degree image

proof.text: The path $\gamma$ is natural for every morphism of covers by [def-real-boundary-decomposition-path], in particular $\gamma_{P_L}(b_L)_{\bar\eta_s}=(b_L)_{\bar u}\gamma_{P_L}$. The formula in [lem-real-boundary-decomposition-landing] now gives $\theta_s(\sigma)_{P_L}=\gamma_{P_L}a_{\sigma,P_L}\gamma_{P_L}^{-1}=(b_L)_{\bar u}$. At $\bar u$, identify the fibre with $\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0}(L,k)$ using the constants map of $\bar u$. The deck transformation sends $\mu$ to $\mu\rho=g\mu$, again because the finite-field Galois group is cyclic. Apply [lem-wf-arithmetic-lift-fibre-path] with $Y_0=U_0$, $K=k_0$, $L=k$: Step 2 verifies its finite-type, separated and geometrically connected hypotheses, and $k_0$ is perfect since its finite algebraic extensions are separable. Its constant-cover characterization gives $p(\theta_s(\sigma))|_L=g|_L$. These equalities for every finite $L$ imply $p(\theta_s(\sigma))=g$, as $k$ is their union. This proves the square for the given arbitrary path and identification. Surjectivity from Step 6 gives $p(\theta_s(D_s))=\iota_s(G_s)=\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_s)$.
